description: Stage-to-agent mapping for faylo-sdlc, organized into 6 phases: Planning & Requirements, Design & Prototyping, Development, Testing & Security, Infrastructure & Deployment, Operations & Monitoring. Stage 01 is optional and tier-gated. Stages 02-06 run automatically back to back from a single one-line request, with no manual document authoring in between. Stages 07-12 run per ticket (07 conditional on UI surface), gated only where the tier faylo-architect assigned actually requires it. Stage 13 runs continuously post-release and closes the loop by feeding new work items back into Stage 01. `specialist_routing` and `triggers` below are the single source of truth for routing and failure hand-off -- agent files reference them rather than keeping their own copies (see AGENT-CONTRACT-SPEC.md).

stages.gate: runs once per existing codebase, before any `start`; `faylo adopt` writes the baseline, the agents write the as-is documents; in-flight stories take precedence in `faylo next`
none by default — triggered only when the one-liner is ambiguous or provisional tier is async-review/hard-gate; skipped otherwise, straight to 02
none — derived automatically from the BRD
none — derived automatically from the PRD
conditional — runs only for tickets faylo-architect flags with a UI surface
none — continuous; can open a new engagement fed back into Stage 01

triggers_doc: Read by `faylo route <stage> <story>` after a stage's command fails: it logs the failure, re-invokes `on_fail` while attempts <= `max_retries`, and otherwise moves the story to Blocked and defers a decision to a human. `on_new_work_item` is where Stage 13 output re-enters the pipeline (`faylo new epic`). Every firing is in the ledger, so `faylo history --summary` reflects it.
